episode_title: Curiosity, Courage, and Building a Business on Your Own Terms

real_qa.q: What did Kathy Loughman do when doctors told her over 85% of children born at less than 28 weeks do not survive?
real_qa.r: When doctors told Kathy that over 85% of children born at less than 28 weeks do not survive, she reframed it by saying "so 15% of them live" and declared "I'm choosing 15." From that moment on, she became what she calls a "driven possibilitarian," focusing on how to make it possible for her daughter to be in the 15% who survive and thrive, rather than accepting the grim statistics.

real_qa.q: What is the core difference between capitalism and commerce according to Becky Molenkamp?
real_qa.r: Becky Molenkamp distinguishes capitalism from commerce by stating that capitalism is only about "more, more, more" with no concept of enough, while commerce is about asking "What's enough to make you whole?" Commerce focuses on wholeness and enoughness rather than endless growth, whether that exchange is money, potatoes, or time spent helping someone.
real_qa.requete: Becky Molenkamp capitalism commerce difference enough

real_qa.q: How did Miriam Shulman explain why customers hesitate to purchase even when they can afford it?
real_qa.r: Miriam Shulman explained that customers often hesitate not because of price or product quality, but because they do not think themselves worthy of spending money on what they want. She gave the example of hesitating to buy a $400 coach bag not due to the bag's value, but because the buyer does not believe they are worth spending $400 on themselves, which is their true underlying objection.
real_qa.requete: Miriam Shulman customer objections worth spending money

real_qa.q: How did Kira Hartley-Klinger use storytelling to increase sales on Etsy?
real_qa.r: Kira Hartley-Klinger wrote personal essays and stories on her Etsy listing pages about where the fabric came from and her experiences acquiring it, using clever names for the people she encountered at auctions. This personal storytelling element transformed her from just a shop into a source, with customers wanting to create things with items from her shop because they had stories behind them.
real_qa.requete: Kira Hartley-Klinger Etsy storytelling product sales

real_qa.q: What insight did Lydia Knight share about curiosity versus judgment in changing behavior?
real_qa.r: Lydia Knight explained that it is difficult to hold curiosity and judgment at the same time, and if someone feels judged they will remove themselves or hide their behavior rather than change it. By shifting from judgment to curiosity, communication improves and people want to stay around you, which is key to actually helping someone transform their thought patterns and behavior.
real_qa.requete: Lydia Knight curiosity judgment behavior change

real_quote: If you can shift to curiosity instead of judgment, your communication changes and people want to stay around you.
